claims.text: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a strong caloric response but poor structural integrity and a tendency to crack.
The initial alloy has a relatively coarse microstructure.
Controlled post-synthesis thermal aging can induce a fine secondary phase along the alloy's grain boundaries.
The aging-induced secondary phase will be ductile.
Avoiding excessive aging will prevent precipitate coarsening.
Grain-boundary precipitates will strengthen the grain boundaries.
The precipitates will act as crack-deflection or crack-blunting sites.
Crack deflection and grain-boundary strengthening will improve the alloy's crack resistance and mechanical integrity.
Properly controlled aging will leave the bulk phase transition responsible for the caloric effect largely unperturbed.
Aged samples will have higher compressive strength than untreated samples.
A successful treatment should increase compressive strength by at least 15% relative to the untreated control.
The aging treatment will preserve the caloric response to within 10% of the untreated alloy's response.
The proposed benefit is expected to persist during combined applied-field, hydrostatic-pressure, thermal-cycling, and representative mechanical-loading conditions.
Aging conditions that trigger undesirable phase transformations or coarsening would fall outside the hypothesis's valid operating window.
